report.numbers: Expert vs Random 98.4%, vs Greedy 87.3%, vs Filler 97.6%; 0 games hit the 60-turn cap; Expert = Greedy on 22% of 10,990 decisions; first player 65.5% in 200 Expert mirror games, 59.5% in 200 more, 62.5% pooled (Greedy mirror 64%); set positions all 5/5 (Greedy wastes the Crown).
report.expertNote: Expert: determinized play-outs to the end of the game (a sampled-greedy policy on both sides), 300 a decision, successive halving over the candidates (the best two placements of each card by a one-glance score, then the best overall, plus ending the turn).
report.setPositionNote: The spec's free flip (a Crown into a cell touching three enemy 1-edges) is not something a person never gets wrong early in the game: the three cards taken keep their 1-edges toward empty cells and are taken straight back, and Expert-vs-Expert play-outs from that position favoured keeping the Crown. The gate position puts the same flip late, where nothing can take them back.
report.loop: Expert places about one card a turn (1.05) although mana usually allows two or three, and passes in 15% of its turns: every card placed is a target, so the game is a waiting game over who places last next to whom. Flips are cheap and mostly temporary (about 7 a game, many retaken); what lasts is a card whose open edges are high or whose neighbours are full. Crowns are held for the end (played with about 4 empty cells left, and often not at all). The first player scores 62% in Expert mirrors (draws counted as half), and 28% of those games end level on cells.
